newsitem.title: USA: Gasoline surge lifts crude prices, US grades even.
newsitem.headline: Gasoline surge lifts crude prices, US grades even.

text.p: Surging gasoline prices lifted the entire energy complex to stronger values Wednesday morning off highly-supportive inventory data released after the close of Tuesday's business.
September West Texas Intermediate/Cushing ranged 40 cents higher at $20.25-35 a barrel, with the September/October roll at -2 cents.
American Petroleum Institute (API) data showed gasoline stocks dropping 3.17 million barrels and crude levels shedding some 9.7 million barrels.
"The follow-through buying off the API's has been the story," said a crude trader.
Extremely favorable gasoline to crude crack spreads have maintained grade differentials. Sour crudes continued to waver ahead of a possible onslaught of Iraqi crude exports.

Trades were seen for September Postings Plus at $2.02, slightly firmer than Tuesday. Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James talked steady at 26-29 cents over the marker, with West Texas Sour/Midland around $1.35 cents cheaper than September WTI.
